headline: Mistakes to Avoid: Trying to Ignore Persistent Rusty Water
articleBody: When you see rusty water, it's easy to think it's just a temporary thing, but ignoring it can lead to bigger plumbing headaches. One common mistake is simply flushing the faucet for a few minutes and hoping it goes away permanently. While a brief flush can sometimes clear discolored water if it's from the city supply, if it keeps coming back, you're likely dealing with an internal plumbing issue that won't fix itself. Another pitfall is trying DIY solutions without understanding the root cause. Pouring chemicals down drains or attempting to tinker with your water heater without proper knowledge can actually cause more damage to your system or even create safety hazards. People often assume it’s just cosmetic, but rusty water signals corrosion, which weakens pipes and can eventually lead to leaks or even pipe bursts. Delaying professional assessment means these issues get worse, turning a potential repair into a much larger, more expensive replacement job. Don't wait until you have a major leak or no hot water; get a qualified plumber to assess the situation quickly.
